question_specs.target_skill: match one distinctive, supplied test observation to a common solid without relying on appearance alone

generation_guidance.task: Give a compact reference table for four allowed common white solids and their observations with water, iodine, and dilute acid. Present one unknown whose single distinctive result matches exactly one reference, then ask for its identity and the decisive observation.
generation_guidance.required_reasoning: Read the supplied comparison table and match the unknown to the only reference with the same distinctive response.
format_constraints: Use exactly four answer choices A-D with one unambiguously correct answer.
Include all reference observations needed in the item; do not require memorizing a chemical list.
Use one safe, virtual observation such as a blue-black iodine response or visible acid bubbling; do not direct a student to taste or directly smell an unknown.
Keep this a one-step D1 item and do not add a suspect-selection subproblem.
generation_guidance.answer_guardrail: The key must cite the discriminating test result, not visual resemblance, and must not claim that every white powder can be identified by one universal test.

question_specs.target_skill: calculate an Rf value from raw distances and compare a multi-band chromatogram with reference inks

generation_guidance.task: Provide an original text table giving the solvent-front distance and two pigment distances for a questioned ink plus three reference pens run under the same conditions. Ask for both questioned Rf values and the uniquely matching reference pattern.
generation_guidance.required_reasoning: Compute each Rf as pigment travel divided by solvent-front travel, then require both bands to agree within a stated tolerance before associating the questioned ink with a reference.
format_constraints: State that every strip used the same paper, solvent, start line, run time, and units.
Choose distances that yield exact two-decimal Rf values between 0 and 1.
Supply a numeric comparison tolerance and ensure exactly one reference matches both bands.
Do not reproduce a source chromatogram or identify a person solely from an ink association.
generation_guidance.answer_guardrail: Independently recompute both ratios. The explanation must distinguish association of ink patterns from proof that a particular person wrote the questioned document.

question_specs.target_skill: infer a plastic-density interval from float-sink observations and select the only compatible reference polymer

generation_guidance.task: Provide densities for three nonhazardous comparison liquids and a reference table of four recyclable plastics with nonoverlapping density ranges. Give float/sink observations for one unknown and ask for its density bracket, plastic identity, and one limitation.
generation_guidance.required_reasoning: Use float means sample density is lower than liquid density and sink means higher, intersect the resulting inequalities, then match the bracket to one reference range.
format_constraints: Define the float/sink density relationship in the stem so the item tests application rather than recall.
Choose observations that make a nonempty, unique density interval and exactly one compatible plastic.
Do not request or simulate a burn test.
State that trapped air and additives are ignored for the simplified item.
generation_guidance.answer_guardrail: The key must preserve strict inequality directions and describe the result as consistent with the named reference plastic under the stated assumptions, not universal proof of polymer identity.

question_specs.target_skill: combine orthogonal qualitative tests and a mass balance to identify both components of a known two-solid mixture

generation_guidance.task: Give a self-contained reference table for four candidate solids, state that an unknown contains exactly two of them, and provide controlled observations before and after water extraction plus one confirmatory test on the residue or filtrate. Include initial dry mass and recovered component masses. Ask for both components, evidence for each, and a recovery-percent check.
generation_guidance.required_reasoning: Use solubility to separate candidate classes, use a selective follow-up response to identify the insoluble or dissolved component, reject at least one tempting alternative, and calculate total percent recovery as a consistency check rather than as the identity test itself.
format_constraints: All test outcomes for every candidate must be supplied; do not depend on undocumented odor, crystal shape, or brand knowledge.
Ensure the two components are uniquely determined only by combining at least two independent observations.
Choose masses that give an exact recovery percentage between 90% and 100% and explicitly attribute the small loss to transfer or filtration.
Do not use an unsafe procedure or ask students to mix reagents physically in this generated question.
Keep the requested response compact: a component-and-evidence table or no more than two short paragraphs plus one calculation.
The answer field itself must include both components, selective evidence, one rejected alternative, the recovery arithmetic and percentage, and the separation-quality interpretation.
generation_guidance.answer_guardrail: The key must not identify a component from recovery percentage alone. It must connect each named component to a selective observation and treat recovery as a procedure-quality check.

question_specs.target_skill: integrate independent trace evidence, eliminate incompatible suspects, and state a calibrated conclusion that separates association from proof

generation_guidance.task: In fewer than 290 student-facing words, create an original property-damage scenario with exactly three fictional suspects. State that the questioned ink is a mixture of exactly two of three reference inks. Give different solvent-front and band-travel distances, not precomputed Rf values. Supply the Rf formula and inclusive tolerance, and include one co-migrating shared band. Exactly two reference pairs must fit. Add compact class-level fiber and time-stamped access evidence that resolve the competing pairs and leave one suspect not excluded. Ask one integrated question: which suspect is best supported, and how do the measurements and other evidence justify that limited conclusion? Do not enumerate intermediate steps, but require calculations and a defensible chain in the rubric.
generation_guidance.required_reasoning: Calculate and normalize band positions by solvent-front distance; handle tolerance and a co-migrating shared band while enumerating two possible reference-pair unions; recognize that chromatography alone is intentionally ambiguous; then use fiber and time evidence to resolve the competing pairs and eliminate alternatives; finally distinguish association from proof. The answer must require at least two non-obvious choices: correct normalization and correct multi-constraint resolution.
format_constraints: Make the matrix internally sufficient; students must not need external suspect stereotypes, motives, or access assumptions.
Ensure exactly one suspect remains compatible only after all three evidence classes are combined; ink evidence alone must yield exactly two explicitly reportable candidate pairs.
Include one shared chromatography band and one irrelevant scene observation so students must distinguish class/shared evidence from exclusions.

Define Rf = band distance divided by solvent-front distance and define the mixture rule: barring overlap, its chromatogram contains the union of bands in its component inks, within a supplied Rf tolerance.

Use these verified strip measurements exactly: Q solvent front 10.0 cm with bands 2.0, 4.0, 6.0, 8.0 cm; Ref A front 8.0 cm with bands 1.6, 3.2 cm; Ref B front 5.0 cm with bands 3.0, 4.0 cm; Ref C front 10.0 cm with bands 4.0, 6.0, 8.0 cm. With tolerance +/-0.02, exactly A+B and A+C reproduce Q; B+C lacks Q's 0.20 band.

Explicitly map each reference ink to its suspect owner and state that all three pens were kept in a shared supply accessible to others, so an owner's alibi does not remove that ink from a possible mixture.

Ask which person is best supported as the writer/damager, not which owner supplied an ink. Make A common to both possible pairs; Alpha's alibi bears on authorship, while the class fiber and compatibility of A+C support Chen over Baker without proving identity.
Use different solvent-front distances across strips so comparing raw band distances gives a tempting but incorrect result; keep divisions hand-solvable and the entire prompt under 290 words.
Do not scaffold a numbered checklist of intermediate inferences; students must decide to normalize, enumerate pairs, and integrate independent evidence.
Avoid violence, drugs, graphic content, real people, real institutions, and claims that classroom comparisons establish legal guilt.
generation_guidance.answer_guardrail: Use 'cannot be excluded and is best supported as the possible writer' rather than 'proved guilty' or 'the only ink contributor.' Explain that Alpha's alibi excludes Alpha as writer but not use of Alpha's shared pen. The answer field itself must contain the complete ideal response with Rf calculations, both compatible pairs, evidence resolution, rival comparisons, and limitation. Independently verify both unions.
generation_guidance.difficulty_adjudication: Judge the shortest solve using the rubric: choosing Rf normalization, enumerating two unions with a shared band, and separating pen ownership from possible authorship are non-obvious decisions.

release_checks: Confirm every evidence category, allowed material, reagent, and expected skill against the final 2027 Division B Rules Manual plus official corrections and clarifications.

Generate every question, scenario, table, value set, distractor, answer, solution, and rubric with the configured model; retrieved sources may ground scope and science but may not supply copied question content.
Blind-solve each item without its stored answer or solution and require agreement with the key.
Independently recompute all Rf values, density inequalities, masses, recovery percentages, and tolerances.
Reject any item whose unknown or suspect is not uniquely determined by the supplied observations and stated assumptions.
Use association language for class evidence; never present a classroom powder, ink, plastic, hair, fiber, fingerprint-pattern, or tread comparison as proof of legal identity or guilt.
Do not instruct students to taste unknowns, directly smell chemicals, perform undocumented burn tests, or carry out procedures outside the applicable Science Olympiad safety rules.
Reject copied or near-copied source wording, values, diagrams, suspect names, narrative details, and answer choices.
Confirm the final bank contains exactly one D1, two D2, and two D3 items, with no D4 item.
caveats: The public Crime Busters event page listed 2027 current-season resources as coming soon when this spec was prepared; the 2026 rules are historical calibration, not authority for the 2027 release.

Hands-on tournament observations depend on reagent concentration, sample preparation, lighting, equipment, and local procedures. Generated pilot questions should therefore provide observations or validated reference tables rather than pretend that uncontrolled test outcomes are universal.
Many Crime Busters evidence types are class evidence. Conclusions must be calibrated as consistency, exclusion, or best-supported association rather than individual identification or proof of guilt.
The cached BullSO PDFs are useful for structural calibration but contain a distinctive copyrighted scenario and specific values that must not be reproduced.
